findings.reason: The original standalone screenshot renders the formulas correctly but only lists the three masses and the three tails in prose. A conditional-mass bar plot materially clarifies why the inclusive p-value sums the observed bar and all bars to the right, despite the middle outcome having the largest individual mass. This is warranted explanatory art under the expanded diagram scope, not a gap in the proof.

Binomial counts are (2 choose 0)(2 choose 2)=1, (2 choose 1)^2=4, (2 choose 2)(2 choose 0)=1 out of (4 choose 2)=6. Heights 1,4,1 in equally scaled drawing coordinates are labeled 1/6,4/6,1/6; the y-axis ticks use the same scale. Masses sum to 1.

The horizontal coordinates increase from k=0 to k=2; the Example explicitly states that larger K favors the alternative that the first sample success probability exceeds the second. No transition, morphism, or commutativity relation is asserted.
